question.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number Shown on an Argand Diagram in Exponential Form
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059847/assets/83c490278bec718da1338f8926e9d67d2f72909487b9a85bbd386cbf72def2bb.png)

Write the complex number $z$, shown on the Argand diagram above, in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-4+\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{1}{4})| \\  & ≈2.897.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{17}$ and $\theta =2.897$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{17}\,{\text{e}}^{2.897\,\text{i}}.
$$
